title: Twenty First Word First Station Fifth Warning Rejecting Worldly Busyness As An Excuse

questions.question: What problem is being addressed at the start of this passage?
questions.answer: It is dealing with being careless or lazy about worship and the required prayers because of worldly busyness.

questions.question: What excuse is mentioned for neglecting worship?
questions.answer: The excuse is being too busy with work and daily responsibilities.

questions.question: How does the passage compare human beings with animals?
questions.answer: It says humans are above animals in ability, but they should not live only to get food and survival like animals.

questions.question: What is described as the true job of a human being?
questions.answer: A human being should work for an everlasting life and live with a higher purpose.

questions.question: According to the passage, what mistake do many people make with worldly matters?
questions.answer: They get involved in many small and unnecessary things and ignore what matters most.

questions.question: What are two examples of useless information given in the passage?
questions.answer: One is being busy with facts about Saturn’s rings, and the other is learning the number of chickens in America.

questions.question: Why are those examples criticized?
questions.answer: They waste valuable time on things that do not help a person in the most important duties.

questions.question: What example is used to show how foolish a weak excuse can be?
questions.answer: A worker is offered great treasure for only ten minutes of effort but refuses because of a tiny loss in wages.

questions.question: What happens if a person leaves the obligatory prayers while working for livelihood?
questions.answer: The person’s work becomes limited to a small and mostly worldly benefit.

questions.question: What two benefits are found when a person uses rest time for prayer?
questions.answer: Prayer helps both worldly livelihood in a blessed way and the person’s provision for the hereafter.

questions.question: What does the passage ask about the reason for being weak in worship?
questions.answer: It asks whether the reason is too much worldly work or the struggle to earn a living.

questions.question: What answer does the passage give to the idea that a person was made only for this world?
questions.answer: It rejects that idea and teaches that life has a greater purpose than worldly survival.

questions.question: Why is the comparison with a sparrow important?
questions.answer: It shows that even small animals may do better in finding basic food, so human greatness must be in something higher.

questions.question: What higher aim is a person supposed to seek?
questions.answer: A person should seek a lasting and real life, not just temporary worldly gain.

questions.question: According to the passage, how do people often misuse their time?
questions.answer: They spend it chasing side issues and collecting information that does not truly benefit them.

questions.question: What attitude does the passage criticize when speaking about such information?
questions.answer: It criticizes acting as if one will stay in this world for an extremely long time.

questions.question: What is the main point of the worker-and-treasure example?
questions.answer: Giving up a huge benefit to avoid a tiny loss is foolish.

questions.question: In the example, what does the small wage cut represent?
questions.answer: It represents the minor worldly cost or time spent on prayer.

questions.question: What does the orchard stand for in the comparison?
questions.answer: It stands for this world where a person works for provision.

questions.question: How are prayers described during a person’s rest times?
questions.answer: They are described as a means of relief for the soul and rest for the heart.

questions.question: What are the two kinds of provision prayer helps a person gain?
questions.answer: It helps with fruitful worldly earning and with supplies for the hereafter.

questions.question: What kind of self is being spoken to in this passage?
questions.answer: It is the self that is attached too much to worldly life.

questions.question: What question is asked about worldly occupations and prayer?
questions.answer: It asks whether worldly busyness is really the reason a person becomes careless with worship.

questions.question: What does the passage say about many things people call worldly duties?
questions.answer: It says many of them are actually small matters that do not deserve so much attention.

questions.question: What deeper problem is shown by spending too much time on minor topics?
questions.answer: It shows forgetfulness of one’s real purpose and the next life.

questions.question: Why is learning random facts used as an example here?
questions.answer: It shows how people may use their minds and time on things that bring little real benefit.

questions.question: How does the passage answer someone who says earning money keeps him from prayer?
questions.answer: It gives an example showing that losing a little time or money for a much greater gain is not a good excuse.

questions.question: Why is refusing the ten-minute digging job described as foolish?
questions.answer: Because the person would give up a very valuable reward to avoid a tiny loss.

questions.question: What does this teach about skipping prayer for work?
questions.answer: It teaches that missing prayer for a small worldly concern means losing something far greater.

questions.question: What effect do prayers have on the spirit and heart, according to the passage?
questions.answer: They refresh the spirit and give breathing room and relief to the heart.

questions.question: What two “mines” are discovered through prayerful and sincere work?
questions.answer: One is reward connected to what grows, and the other is charity-like reward from what others consume.

questions.question: What main conflict is discussed in this passage?
questions.answer: It discusses the conflict between worldly distractions and faithful worship.

questions.question: What wrong idea about human life is challenged here?
questions.answer: The wrong idea is that people exist only to work for worldly needs.

questions.question: How does the passage use animals to make its point?
questions.answer: It says humans should not lower themselves to living only for food and survival like animals.

questions.question: What does the passage say about many busy activities in life?
questions.answer: It says many of them are not truly necessary and are often unnecessary interference in lesser matters.

questions.question: Why is acting like one will live for a thousand years a problem?
questions.answer: It makes a person put off the most important duties and chase things that do not last.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the example about facts on space and chickens?
questions.answer: It is to show how people can waste precious life on pointless details.

questions.question: What claim does the passage respond to after those examples?
questions.answer: It responds to the claim that prayer is neglected because of necessary work for earning a living.

questions.question: What lesson comes from the offer to dig for ten minutes?
questions.answer: A tiny sacrifice is worth making when the reward is much greater.

questions.question: How is daily work in this world pictured in the comparison?
questions.answer: It is pictured as labor in a garden or orchard for one’s provision.

questions.question: What does abandoning obligatory prayer do to the results of that labor?
questions.answer: It narrows the results down to weak worldly gain only.

questions.question: What extra results can prayer add to a person’s work?
questions.answer: It can add blessing in worldly earnings and reward for the hereafter.

questions.question: Who is being warned in the opening words of this passage?
questions.answer: The warning is directed at the self that loves worldly life too much.

questions.question: What two possible reasons for neglecting worship are mentioned first?
questions.answer: One is having many worldly tasks, and the other is being busy earning a living.

questions.question: What important question is asked about the purpose of human creation?
questions.answer: It asks whether a person was made only for this world.

questions.question: What does the passage say is wrong with living only for worldly needs?
questions.answer: It lowers a human being beneath his real purpose and higher abilities.

questions.question: How does the passage show that worldly busyness is often exaggerated?
questions.answer: It says many so-called duties are actually minor issues people involve themselves in too much.

questions.question: What warning is given through the examples of odd facts and statistics?
questions.answer: A person can waste precious time on things that do not help his true mission.

questions.question: How does the passage treat the excuse of earning a livelihood?
questions.answer: It says that even this excuse fails when compared to the huge value of prayer.

questions.question: In the comparison, why is the worker’s refusal unreasonable?
questions.answer: He would avoid a tiny pay loss while missing a treasure worth much more.

questions.question: What does this comparison suggest about the value of prayer?
questions.answer: Prayer brings benefits so great that leaving it for small worldly reasons is senseless.

questions.question: When are prayers said to fit naturally into a working day?
questions.answer: They fit into rest times when the soul and heart need renewal.

questions.question: What are the two sources of gain found through combining work with prayer?
questions.answer: One helps worldly life in a fruitful way, and the other stores provision for the next life.

questions.question: What weakness in a person’s worship is the passage mainly trying to cure?
questions.answer: It is trying to cure laziness and neglect in the required prayers because of attachment to worldly life.

questions.question: What does the passage say about human ability compared with animals?
questions.answer: Humans have greater abilities, so their lives should aim higher than basic survival.

questions.question: Why is the sparrow mentioned?
questions.answer: It shows that success in getting food is not what makes humans truly special.

questions.question: What is the lasting goal a person should work for?
questions.answer: He should work for a real and lasting life beyond this temporary world.

questions.question: What does the passage say about many things people get busy with?
questions.answer: Many are side matters that people treat as important when they are not.

questions.question: What is the danger of filling life with needless information?
questions.answer: It wastes time that should be used for more important duties and preparation.

questions.question: What example is given to show the weakness of the livelihood excuse?
questions.answer: The example of a laborer refusing a short task that would lead to a very valuable reward.

questions.question: What does the orchard symbolize in that example?
questions.answer: It symbolizes a person’s place of work in worldly life.

questions.question: If a person drops the required prayers, how are the results of his work described?
questions.answer: They remain small, worldly, and lacking deeper fruit.

questions.question: What good use of break time does the passage recommend?
questions.answer: It recommends using it for prayer so the inner self can rest and recover.

questions.question: What are the two major gains connected with prayer and work together?
questions.answer: They bring blessed worldly provision and reward for the life after death.

questions.question: How does sincere intention affect ordinary labor?
questions.answer: It can turn ordinary labor into something that earns spiritual reward.

questions.question: Under what view of oneself can feeding others become reward like charity?
questions.answer: When a person sees himself as a servant delivering Allah’s property to His creation.
